Second Year Semester IV Course: Holistic Wellness, Resilience and Mindfulness Course Identification Table Particular Details Course Code CC-HW-229 Course Title Holistic Wellness, Resilience and Mindfulness Course Category Co-Curricular (CC) Course Nature of Course Practical and Activity-Oriented Credit Distribution 2 (Practical) Practical Marks 50 Marks Instructional Hours 60 Clock Hours Medium of Instruction: English and Marathi Accessibility Provisions ISL-supported instruction, captions, visual learning materials and accessible assessment options, wherever appropriate Introduction Section Content Introduction This course introduces students to holistic wellness as a practical and inclusive learning process connected with physical wellbeing, emotional balance, resilience, mindfulness, healthy routines, and life skills. It enables learners to understand wellness through activity -based learning, observation, reflection, guided practice, and practical application in everyday ...

units.title: Understanding Holistic Wellness and Healthy Living
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning and concept of holistic wellness in physical, emotional, mental, social, and ethical dimensions. 1.2 Wellness in student life: self -care, balance, discipline, and healthy habits. 1.3 Inclusive wellbeing in educational spaces and diverse classrooms. 1.4 Awareness of sleep, food, movement, rest, and personal hygiene as part of healthy living. 1.5 Wellness as an individual, social, and institutional responsibility.

units.title: Stress, Emotions, and Resilience in Student Life
units.topics: 2.1 Meaning and sources of stress in academic, personal, and social life. 2.2 Emotional health, self -esteem, self -expression, and coping with pressure. 2.3 Resilience: meaning, importance, and practical development through daily habits. 2.4 Time management, exam pressure, adjustment, and help -seeking behaviour. 2.5 Peer support, guidance systems, and positive response to difficulties.

units.title: Mindfulness, Self-Awareness, and Reflective Practice
units.topics: 3.1 Meaning of mindfulness and present-moment awareness. 12 3.2 Self-awareness, reflection, and emotional regulation in everyday life. 3.3 Breathing, relaxation, stretching, and simple mindfulness practices. 3.4 Gratitude, positive thinking, calm response, and reflective living. 3.5 Use of journals, guided reflection, and self-monitoring for personal growth.

units.title: Inclusive Wellbeing, Digital Balance, and Practical Wellness
units.topics: Action 4.1 Respect for diversity, disability inclusion, accessibility, dignity, and supportive relationships. 4.2 Healthy communication, empathy, mutual support, and wellbeing in inclusive classrooms. 4.3 Digital wellbeing and healthy use of mobile phones, internet, and social media. 4.4 Managing distraction, overuse, emotional fatigue, and unhealthy digital habits. 4.5 Preparation of personal wellness plans, awareness activities, portfolio work, and final practical presentation.

units.title: Maintain a wellness diary for one or two weeks based on sleep, food, mood, activity, and digital habits.
